name: Major cyber incidents
value: EU cold-chain attacks; US advisory 5 Nov
summary: Refrigeration-control attacks spread across Europe and reached French blood banks; US agencies issued a warning 5 Nov
state: A second wave of attacks on refrigeration controls hit shops in several European countries from 2 Nov (Help Net Security). Cold rooms at three French Blood Establishment sites were tampered with via a supplier, with no loss of blood products reported (BleepingComputer). Five US agencies warned of attacks on grocery and cold-storage controls on 5 Nov, naming no culprit (Nextgov). The FBI attributed the $6.34bn Binance theft of 29 Oct to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, a financial rather than destructive attack. No national-scale outage of power, health or finance had been found as of 8 Nov.
for_you: Food retailers, cold-storage operators and health bodies with internet-exposed refrigeration controls are most exposed. Shoppers may see discarded chilled stock where stores are hit.
rubric_hit: Watch: attacks disrupting large retailers and a critical service. Alert line not met: no national-scale attack on power, health or finance, and no destructive state-attributed attack.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
